CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. The patient reports that the injury occurred on Sunday while skiing, approximately 4 days ago. She was attempting moguls and her strap became caught on her finger, causing it to bend backwards (hyperextension). The pain is exacerbated by movement, particularly with bending. She has tried ice and ibuprofen, but the pain remains severe.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with finger movement. Otherwise not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation (recent). Appendectomy at age 18.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation. Ibuprofen for finger pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger exam reveals tenderness over the distal phalanx and distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over the proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Patient able to bend, extend, and touch thumb with finger. Pain noted with flexion.

RESULTS
X-rays of right index finger show no fractures. Normal alignment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion on the tip of the finger. Recommended aluminum foam splint and Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately one week. Patient to follow up if symptoms do not improve.
